o1.biggest_strength: Every email follows from what the user just did: email 3 fires after the recurring task, skip rules stop repeats, and the holdout is honest that the data shows a link to retention, not cause.
o1.biggest_mistake: It drops the team-invite email but brings sharing back as email 5, sent to everyone on a fixed day, even though shared projects retain worst (34%) and reach only 6% of users.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the share email with one that deepens the two key habits or helps users with both, and pick one subject line per email instead of listing '(test: ...)' alternates.

o2.biggest_strength: A clean, ready-to-load series built on the two habits, with platform branching, a guilt-free check-in, and a goal and measure for every email, plus a Pro email sent at day 14 only to users who have formed a habit.
o2.biggest_mistake: The Pro email rests on the claim that time-based reminders are a Pro feature, which needs checking before it goes to customers. Email 3 is sent on a fixed day 3 even though the 'recurring task created' trigger was available.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Confirm the Pro feature claim, and send the second-device email right after the recurring task is created so the two habits stack.

reason: Both are strong and on-brand. I'd take the second because it drops team sharing entirely, saves Pro for people already getting value, and is cleaner to hand to the team. The first has smarter trigger chaining but slips a sharing email back in.
